cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Players note display resolution snags and awkward keyboard layouts.

claims.claim: Mouse and keyboard controls feel awkward and aim sensitivity can feel off.

citations.review_text:
I recommend this only because It's still better than the other games that want to nickel and dime you. Yes, this version was slapped together with (deliberate?) issues (to frustrate you into buying another product?). Those issues honestly aren't that bad though. I played a galactic conquest and the campaign, and the only really weird thing was that sometimes the AI will be completely idiotic (and that probably is just a holdover from the original edition, which I played for hundreds of hours). You'll also have to configure all of the controls (like the default to enter a vehicle is "enter," but the game UI tells you it's "E"). Thankfully, this is a game that does let you map every button and function. Being able to turn faster with the mouse does seem to break the AATs though (they almost fly off the ground when you turn fast, but the AATs were already too nerfed in BF II to want to use. Tanks were OP in BF I, but in BF II, even on normal mode every NPC is going to throw all of their grenades at you while you're just waiting for your weapons to cool down). 

The only really regrettable part of this port is monitor support. When you have multiple monitors, it's gonna pick which monitor it wants to run on, so you basically have to unplug the monitor you don't want to play on if you don't like the monitor it picks. It also isn't capable of ultrawide aspect ratios. 

Remember, kids. P1r8ing is bad.

Recommend this game to anyone who played it decades ago. Gameplay holds up really well even now 21 years later. Only problems I really have is how awkward M&K can be when playing this game. Adjusted mouse sensitivity but it always feels slightly "off" when I try to aim or snap to targets. Also had it crash twice on the Mustafar campaign level for whatever reason but functioned well afterwards. Would also be nice if there was support for controller but that doesn't break the experience overall. Recommend people to pick it up if only to experience how much better this older iteration of SW:Battlefront is versus the newer ones that released.

claims.claim: The port has display and aspect ratio issues, including improper handling of ultrawide resolutions and forcing users to unplug secondary displays on multi-monitor setups to control which screen the game launches on.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Battlers describe multiplayer connectivity lag and display conflicts.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe experiencing severe lag and connectivity issues when playing multiplayer matches.

citations.review_text: Just said no because there is no middle option. The game works fine single player, multiplayer is an entirely different story. I can play a 2v2 multiplayer game with a host who is like 10 miles away from me with the same ISP and the lag and connectivity issues are severe. The game crashed for me once and activated my Windows Defender program. For some strange reason though, Battlefront 1 works perfectly fine with multiplayer.

Play this instead of the EA titles if you're after a large-scale shooter in the Star Wars universe. Sure, the graphics look a little crusty these days, but this was actually made by people who cared. I'd avoid the multiplayer unless you like getting obliterated by shotguns and detpacks though. The modding scene is pretty cool too.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that running Discord causes the game screen to appear black.

citations.review_text: Screen is black when discord is running. Otherwise, 10/10

THIS IS ACTUALLY A GOOD GAME! the only reason I said "do not recommend" is because for the past few months I've been dealing with a really weird glitch in which the game just will not launch, I've started troubleshooting again, if I fix it I'll change the review to positive and edit the solution to the end
The game itself is really well made and holds up remarkably well, I'd even prefer it over it's 2017 reboot game, the game modes I enjoy most are instant action with every map and mode enabled at random and galactic conquest (note I never played online because frankly I didn't want to) I think the place where this game shines the most are the community mods, like the remaster mod or legends content. the only thing that has bugged me about this game (aside from it not launching) is that each faction on each map is locked to one hero (unless you're playing hero assault), but that's more of a nitpick because I like the lightsaber characters and would get slightly disappointed when I would get Boba or Jango Fett instead of Grevious or Vader.
The issue was that files were missing and I found that out after trying t0o run the game as administrator, I looked up the files that were missing and had to repair/redownload Microsoft Visual C++

claims.claim: Reviewers note that certain maps advantage one team over the other regarding vehicle availability or sniper positions, and online multiplayer matches can suffer from lag for non-host players.

citations.review_text:
English Version (french below) : 

Absolute banger : classic Capture The Flag (CTF), a galactic conquest game mode, lots of different maps, classes and heroes to choose from across different eras and even space battles that let you invade the enemy's flagship and sabotage it from the inside ? All of this with a singleplayer campaign that is actually interesting and dives into the role of clones turning into the first Empire's solidiers ? 

Ok now, some maps can be really advantageous to one team depening on the available vehicles or good spots for snipers, and some heroes are definitely better than others, so the game is definitely not perfect and sometimes the controls can feel a bit clunky, but the game is cleary a banger. 
The only criminal flaw is not letting galactic conquest be multiplayer, I mean why ? 



Version Française : 

Un banger absolu : des parties de capture de drapeaux classiques, un mode de conquête galactique, plein de maps, classes et héros de différentes époques de la saga et même des batailles spatiales qui vous laissent aborder le vaisseau amiral ennemi pour le saboter de l'intérieur ? Le tout avec une campagne solo vraiment intéressante qui se concentre sur l'état d'esprit des clones qui sont devenus les premiers soldats de l'Empire ?

Bon maintenant, certaines maps avantagent clairement un camp plutôt que l'autre, que ce soit au niveau des véhicules disponibles, des spots pour les snipers ou des héros disponibles (parce que certains sont clairement meilleurs que d'autre). Les contrôles peuvent être un peu bancal par moment, mais le jeu est clairement archi cool.
Le seul crime, c'est que le mode conquête galactique ne soit pas jouable en multijoueur, je veux dire... pourquoi ?

9/10

Only thing holding it back is the lower graphics, confusing ways to be able to use mods and a lot of the weapons and starfighters are pretty inaccurate to how they are in the lore 
(V-wing as the bomber but the ARC-170 as the standard fighter is the most notable example along with pretty lazy reload animations for blasters which idk if they even need to reload or not)

SWBF2 isn't their to be 100% accurate nor the most pretty, it's their to be one of the most replayable Star Wars video game out their and it does that wonderfully well. The Classes are mostly balanced outside of the CIS and more importantly you can freely hop in and out of vehicles like in Halo which is a insane quality of life feature you don't get to see in a lot of videogames sadly.

While multiplayer is a bit laggy the fact we even got multiplayer support after all the years is a HUGE W but otherwise I'd treat this mostly as a singleplayer game like Star Wars Empire at War.

Even to someone who is not familiar with Star Wars outside of showing them the main 6 movies this is probably one of the best games you could introduce them into the genre outside of Republic Commando itself but unlike Republic Commando it has more replayability because of stuff like Galactic Conquest and multiplayer which Republic Commando lacks sadly.

If your a Star Wars fan this game is a must whether your more into the Galactic Civil War period or the Clone Wars this game has it all, even for all you Old Republic fans the mods got you covered so long as you can put up with the bureaucracy of learning how the hell to install them.

Absolute banger. Nothing else on the market quite like it.

Arguably a significant improvement from the first game in terms of pacing and the smootheness of the gameplay, albeit at the expense of factions more or less being re-skins of each other. The maps and factions are more balanced than in Battlefront I, though often still heavily favor one side over the other. The game shows its age but holds itself up quite well for a retro game; I am partial to the lack of microtransactions and the heavier emphasis on strategic gameplay in Conquest mode in contrast to the typical "shoot x number of enemies" gameplay that underwhelms me in most shooters.

The online community is more alive and approachable than the Battlefront I community in my experience. With the game being as dated as it is, whether or not shots hit at all in online gameplay is a mix of skill, fortune, and ping which takes some getting used to. The modding community also grants loads of free content for the game.

Truly an amazing game. I have been playing this game since I was a kid. I was playing the original Battlefront even before this one. What is amazing is how well this game stands the test of time. Still doesn't feel antiquated at all. Still one of the best games. Unfortunately, the online on PC is a laggy mess for anyone that is not the host. Which makes few want to play.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the singleplayer campaign as interesting, featuring elements like clone trooper perspectives, fetch quests, and defeating more enemies than they kill.

citations.review_text:
English Version (french below) : 

Absolute banger : classic Capture The Flag (CTF), a galactic conquest game mode, lots of different maps, classes and heroes to choose from across different eras and even space battles that let you invade the enemy's flagship and sabotage it from the inside ? All of this with a singleplayer campaign that is actually interesting and dives into the role of clones turning into the first Empire's solidiers ? 

Ok now, some maps can be really advantageous to one team depening on the available vehicles or good spots for snipers, and some heroes are definitely better than others, so the game is definitely not perfect and sometimes the controls can feel a bit clunky, but the game is cleary a banger. 
The only criminal flaw is not letting galactic conquest be multiplayer, I mean why ? 



Version Française : 

Un banger absolu : des parties de capture de drapeaux classiques, un mode de conquête galactique, plein de maps, classes et héros de différentes époques de la saga et même des batailles spatiales qui vous laissent aborder le vaisseau amiral ennemi pour le saboter de l'intérieur ? Le tout avec une campagne solo vraiment intéressante qui se concentre sur l'état d'esprit des clones qui sont devenus les premiers soldats de l'Empire ?

Bon maintenant, certaines maps avantagent clairement un camp plutôt que l'autre, que ce soit au niveau des véhicules disponibles, des spots pour les snipers ou des héros disponibles (parce que certains sont clairement meilleurs que d'autre). Les contrôles peuvent être un peu bancal par moment, mais le jeu est clairement archi cool.
Le seul crime, c'est que le mode conquête galactique ne soit pas jouable en multijoueur, je veux dire... pourquoi ?

Still the better one of "battlefront II". Sure the graphic might be dated and NPCs are clunky but not only can I conquer the galaxy with my chosen faction but it has an interesting and engaging single player story. (Though I have to admit it's just fetch quests and kill more enemies than they can kill your guys... though that's what we're here for!)
It also runs better on older machines and you don't need internet access all the time.
